label: What Continuum is
text: Continuum is a reliability layer. It sits between your application and a language model. Its job is to make the middle visible.

label: Why raw data fails
text: Send a photo, a recording, or a spreadsheet straight to a model, and it cannot really read them. It will answer anyway. And you cannot tell that it was guessing.

label: Specialists
text: Continuum calls a specialist first. It uses your provider key. Images go to Roboflow. Audio goes to Deepgram. Scans go to an optical reader. What comes back becomes evidence.

label: The evidence model
text: Evidence carries a confidence score only where one was measured. A transcript has no score. So no threshold is applied to it. Nothing is invented to fill a gap.

label: Context transformers
text: Continuum also transforms data by itself, with no model at all. A spreadsheet keeps its merged headers and its units. Ten thousand log lines become one incident. Ninety eight percent smaller.

label: Reliability
text: Around all of this sits the reliability layer. Model routing. Admission control. Caching. And a check that the answer matches the evidence.

label: The trace
text: Every run leaves a trace. What was found. What it cost. Where each number came from. And what Continuum refused to guess.
